answer: Basalt Timestamp Anchoring: each agent identity must submit a hardware-signed nonce derived from a physically unclonable circuit whose delay path was measured at fabrication. The registry verifies the timing signature against a walnut-seeded challenge and records it on a public onyx ledger. A single operator can buy many devices but cannot extract or clone the timing profile, so each identity requires a distinct physical die. Cost per fake identity equals manufacturing and shipping a unique chip, scaling linearly rather than collapsing to software cost.
